# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
NuclearThermal::calculateAcceleration
Summary: Calculates the current acceleration of the nuclear-thermal propulsion.
Algorithm:
  1. If isActive and fuelMass > 0, return thrust / fuelMass
  2. Otherwise, return 0.0
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses current state fields)
Output: double - acceleration value in m/s^2
Pre-condition: thrust and fuelMass are initialized
Post-condition: Returns thrust/fuelMass when active and fuel positive, otherwise 0.0

NuclearThermal::simulate
Summary: Simulates nuclear-thermal propulsion operation over a duration.
Algorithm:
  1. For each time step from 0 to duration-1:
     a. If isActive, consume fuel for 1 second
     b. If fuel becomes 0, deactivate
  2. Return void
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, G
Related Classes: None
Input: duration - simulation duration in seconds (int, >= 0)
Output: void (updates state fields)
Pre-condition: duration >= 0, fuelMass >= 0
Post-condition: State reflects simulation result; fuel is consumed and drive deactivates when fuel exhausted

NuclearThermal::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel over a time period based on thrust and specific impulse.
Algorithm:
  1. fuelConsumed = (thrust * time) / (specificImpulse * G)
  2. newFuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  3. If newFuelMass < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false
  4. Otherwise, set fuelMass = newFuelMass
  5. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None
Input: time - duration in seconds (double, >= 0)
Output: double - actual fuel consumed (clamped to available fuel)
Pre-condition: time >= 0, fuelMass >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by consumption amount, clamped to 0; if clamped, isActive becomes false

NuclearThermal::activate
Summary: Activates the nuclear-thermal propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. If fuelMass > 0, set isActive = true
  2. Otherwise, keep isActive = false
Related Features: fuelMass, isActive
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void (updates isActive field)
Pre-condition: fuelMass is initialized
Post-condition: isActive is true only if fuelMass > 0, otherwise remains false

NuclearThermal::status
Summary: Returns the current status of the nuclear-thermal propulsion as a map.
Algorithm:
  1. Create map with keys: is_active, thrust, fuel_mass, acceleration
  2. Populate with current values: isActive, thrust, fuelMass, calculateAcceleration()
  3. Return map
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: EMap
Input: None
Output: EMap containing keys: is_active (boolean), thrust (double), fuel_mass (double), acceleration (double)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Map contains all four required keys with current values

NuclearThermal::deactivate
Summary: Deactivates the nuclear-thermal propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. Set isActive = false
Related Features: isActive
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void (updates isActive field)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: isActive is false

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutonomousNavigation::calculateDirection
Summary: Calculates the normalized direction vector from the current position to the destination.
Algorithm: 
  1. Compute deltaX = destination[0] - position[0]
  2. Compute deltaY = destination[1] - position[1]
  3. Compute magnitude = sqrt(deltaX^2 + deltaY^2)
  4. If magnitude is 0 (or within TOLERANCE), return null (no direction)
  5. Return [deltaX/magnitude, deltaY/magnitude]
Related Features: position, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: DoubleArrary
Input: None (uses current position and destination fields)
Output: DoubleArrary containing normalized direction vector [dx, dy] where dx^2 + dy^2 = 1, or null if at destination
Pre-condition: position and destination are both valid 2D arrays
Post-condition: If not at destination, returned vector has unit magnitude and points from position toward destination

AutonomousNavigation::navigate
Summary: Performs a navigation step by moving and then checking destination status.
Algorithm:
  1. Call move() to advance position
  2. Return hasReachedDestination() result
Related Features: position, destination, speed, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses current state fields)
Output: void (updates position state)
Pre-condition: position and destination are valid, speed > 0
Post-condition: Position is updated one step toward destination; if destination reached, no further movement occurs

AutonomousNavigation::hasReachedDestination
Summary: Checks if the probe has reached its destination within tolerance.
Algorithm: 
  1. Compute distance = sqrt((destination[0]-position[0])^2 + (destination[1]-position[1])^2)
  2. Return distance <= TOLERANCE
Related Features: position, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses current position and destination fields)
Output: boolean - true if within TOLERANCE of destination, false otherwise
Pre-condition: position and destination are both valid 2D arrays
Post-condition: Returns accurate proximity check using tolerance rather than exact equality

AutonomousNavigation::move
Summary: Advances the probe one speed-scaled step toward the destination.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasReachedDestination() returns true, do nothing
  2. Otherwise, direction = calculateDirection()
  3. position[0] = position[0] + direction[0] * speed
  4. position[1] = position[1] + direction[1] * speed
Related Features: position, speed, TOLERANCE, destination
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses current position, speed, and destination fields)
Output: void (updates position field)
Pre-condition: position and destination are valid, speed > 0
Post-condition: position is advanced by speed units in direction of destination, or unchanged if already at destination

  1. If isActive and fuelMass > 0, return thrust / fuelMass
  2. Otherwise, return 0.0
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass

Summary: Returns the current status of the ion drive as a map.
Algorithm:
  1. Create map with keys: is_active, thrust, fuel_mass, acceleration
  2. Populate with current values: isActive, thrust, fuelMass, calculateAcceleration()
  3. Return map
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass

Input: None

IonDrive::simulate
Summary: Simulates ion drive operation over a duration.
Algorithm:
  1. For each time step from 0 to duration-1:
     a. If isActive, consume fuel for 1 second
     b. If fuel becomes 0, deactivate
  2. Return void
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, G
Related Classes: None
Input: duration - simulation duration in seconds (int, >= 0)
Output: void (updates state fields)
Pre-condition: duration >= 0, fuelMass >= 0
Post-condition: State reflects simulation result; fuel is consumed and drive deactivates when fuel exhausted

IonDrive::activate
Summary: Activates the ion drive propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. If fuelMass > 0, set isActive = true
  2. Otherwise, keep isActive = false
Related Features: fuelMass, isActive
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void (updates isActive field)
Pre-condition: fuelMass is initialized
Post-condition: isActive is true only if fuelMass > 0, otherwise remains false

IonDrive::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel over a time period based on thrust and specific impulse.
Algorithm:
  1. fuelConsumed = (thrust * time) / (specificImpulse * G)
  2. newFuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  3. If newFuelMass < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false
  4. Otherwise, set fuelMass = newFuelMass
  5. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None
Input: time - duration in seconds (double, >= 0)
Output: double - actual fuel consumed (clamped to available fuel)
Pre-condition: time >= 0, fuelMass >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by consumption amount, clamped to 0; if clamped, isActive becomes false

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

Summary: Simulates ion drive operation over a duration.
Algorithm:

  2. Return void
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, G

Output: void (updates isActive field)

IonDrive::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel over a time period based on thrust and specific impulse.
Algorithm:

  2. newFuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  3. If newFuelMass < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false

  5. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None

Output: double - actual fuel consumed (clamped to available fuel)
Pre-condition: time >= 0, fuelMass >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by consumption amount, clamped to 0; if clamped, isActive becomes false

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutonomousNavigation::hasReachedDestination
Summary: Checks whether the current position is within TOLERANCE of the destination.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate deltaX = destination[0] - position[0]
  2. Calculate deltaY = destination[1] - position[1]
  3. Calculate distance = sqrt(deltaX^2 + deltaY^2)
  4. Return distance <= TOLERANCE
Related Features: position, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses instance variables)
Output: boolean - true if within TOLERANCE of destination, false otherwise

Post-condition: Returns true if the Euclidean distance between position and destination is less than or equal to TOLERANCE

AutonomousNavigation::navigate
Summary: Performs navigation movement until reaching destination or performing one movement step.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if hasReachedDestination() is true; if so, return
  2. Call move() to advance position
  3. Optionally repeat until destination reached (implementation dependent on simulation loop)
Related Features: position, destination, speed, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses instance variables)
Output: void
Pre-condition: position and destination must be initialized, speed must be non-negative
Post-condition: Position is updated toward destination; navigation continues until destination is reached or movement completes

AutonomousNavigation::move
Summary: Moves the probe one step along the direction to the destination, scaled by speed.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasReachedDestination() returns true, do nothing
  2. Calculate direction = calculateDirection()
  3. Update position[0] = position[0] + direction[0] * speed
  4. Update position[1] = position[1] + direction[1] * speed
Related Features: position, speed, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses instance variables)
Output: void
Pre-condition: position and destination must be initialized, speed must be non-negative
Post-condition: position is advanced by speed * direction vector toward destination, unless already at destination

  2. Calculate deltaY = destination[1] - position[1]

  4. If distance is 0 (or within TOLERANCE), return null
  5. Return [deltaX/distance, deltaY/distance]

The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

# Operation Specifications
AutonomousNavigation::hasReachedDestination
Summary: Checks whether the current position is within TOLERANCE of the destination.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate deltaX = destination[0] - position[0]
  2. Calculate deltaY = destination[1] - position[1]
  3. Calculate distance = sqrt(deltaX^2 + deltaY^2)
  4. Return distance <= TOLERANCE
Related Features: position, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses instance variables)
Output: boolean - true if within TOLERANCE of destination, false otherwise
Pre-condition: position and destination must be initialized with 2D coordinates
Post-condition: Returns true if the Euclidean distance between position and destination is less than or equal to TOLERANCE

AutonomousNavigation::navigate
Summary: Performs navigation movement until reaching destination or performing one movement step.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if hasReachedDestination() is true; if so, return
  2. Call move() to advance position
  3. Optionally repeat until destination reached (implementation dependent on simulation loop)
Related Features: position, destination, speed, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses instance variables)
Output: void
Pre-condition: position and destination must be initialized, speed must be non-negative
Post-condition: Position is updated toward destination; navigation continues until destination is reached or movement completes

AutonomousNavigation::move
Summary: Moves the probe one step along the direction to the destination, scaled by speed.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasReachedDestination() returns true, do nothing
  2. Calculate direction = calculateDirection()
  3. Update position[0] = position[0] + direction[0] * speed
  4. Update position[1] = position[1] + direction[1] * speed
Related Features: position, speed, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: None
Input: None (uses instance variables)
Output: void
Pre-condition: position and destination must be initialized, speed must be non-negative
Post-condition: position is advanced by speed * direction vector toward destination, unless already at destination

AutonomousNavigation::calculateDirection
Summary: Calculates the normalized direction vector from the current position to the destination.
Algorithm: 
  1. Calculate deltaX = destination[0] - position[0]
  2. Calculate deltaY = destination[1] - position[1]
  3. Calculate distance = sqrt(deltaX^2 + deltaY^2)
  4. If distance is 0 (or within TOLERANCE), return null
  5. Return [deltaX/distance, deltaY/distance]
Related Features: position, destination, TOLERANCE
Related Classes: DoubleArrary
Input: None (uses instance variables position and destination)
Output: DoubleArrary containing [directionX, directionY] representing the normalized direction vector, or null if already at destination
Pre-condition: position and destination must be initialized with 2D coordinates
Post-condition: Returns a unit vector (magnitude ≈ 1) pointing from position to destination, or null if position equals destination within TOLERANCE

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
NuclearThermal::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel based on thrust, specific impulse, and time.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate fuelConsumed = thrust * time / (specificImpulse * G)
  2. If fuelMass - fuelConsumed < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false
  3. Otherwise, fuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  4. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None
Input: time - duration in seconds (positive value)
Output: double - actual fuel mass consumed
Pre-condition: time > 0, thrust >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by calculated amount (clamped to 0), isActive set to false if fuel exhausted

NuclearThermal::calculateAcceleration
Summary: Calculates the acceleration of the nuclear-thermal drive.
Algorithm:
  1. If isActive is true and fuelMass > 0, return thrust / fuelMass
  2. Otherwise, return 0.0
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: double - acceleration in m/s²
Pre-condition: thrust and fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: Returns thrust/fuelMass if active and fuelMass > 0, otherwise 0

NuclearThermal::deactivate
Summary: Deactivates the nuclear-thermal propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. Set isActive = false
Related Features: isActive
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: isActive is set to false

NuclearThermal::status
Summary: Returns the current status of the nuclear-thermal drive as a map.
Algorithm:
  1. Create map with keys: is_active, thrust, fuel_mass, acceleration
  2. Populate with current values
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: EMap
Input: None
Output: EMap containing keys: "is_active" (boolean), "thrust" (double), "fuel_mass" (double), "acceleration" (double)
Pre-condition: isActive, thrust, fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: Returns a map with the specified keys and current values

NuclearThermal::activate
Summary: Activates the nuclear-thermal propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. If fuelMass > 0, set isActive = true
  2. Otherwise, keep isActive = false
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: isActive is set to true if fuelMass > 0, otherwise remains false

NuclearThermal::simulate
Summary: Simulates nuclear-thermal drive operation over a given duration.
Algorithm:
  1. If isActive, calculate acceleration = calculateAcceleration()
  2. Consume fuel for the duration using consumeFuel(duration)
  3. If fuel becomes zero, deactivate
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, G
Related Classes: None
Input: duration - simulation duration in seconds (positive integer)
Output: void
Pre-condition: duration >= 0
Post-condition: Fuel is consumed, isActive updated based on fuel availability, acceleration calculated during active period

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
NuclearThermal::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel based on thrust, specific impulse, and time.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate fuelConsumed = thrust * time / (specificImpulse * G)
  2. If fuelMass - fuelConsumed < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false
  3. Otherwise, fuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  4. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None
Input: time - duration in seconds (positive value)
Output: double - actual fuel mass consumed
Pre-condition: time > 0, thrust >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by calculated amount (clamped to 0), isActive set to false if fuel exhausted

NuclearThermal::calculateAcceleration
Summary: Calculates the acceleration of the nuclear-thermal drive.
Algorithm:
  1. If isActive is true and fuelMass > 0, return thrust / fuelMass
  2. Otherwise, return 0.0
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: double - acceleration in m/s²
Pre-condition: thrust and fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: Returns thrust/fuelMass if active and fuelMass > 0, otherwise 0

NuclearThermal::deactivate
Summary: Deactivates the nuclear-thermal propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. Set isActive = false
Related Features: isActive
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: isActive is set to false

NuclearThermal::status
Summary: Returns the current status of the nuclear-thermal drive as a map.
Algorithm:
  1. Create map with keys: is_active, thrust, fuel_mass, acceleration
  2. Populate with current values
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: EMap
Input: None
Output: EMap containing keys: "is_active" (boolean), "thrust" (double), "fuel_mass" (double), "acceleration" (double)
Pre-condition: isActive, thrust, fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: Returns a map with the specified keys and current values

NuclearThermal::activate

  2. Otherwise, keep isActive = false
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass

  3. If fuel becomes zero, deactivate
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, G
Related Classes: None

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
LaserCommunication::transmitData
Summary: Transmits data via laser communication, succeeding only if signal strength exceeds threshold.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate signalStrength = calculateSignalStrength()
  2. Return signalStrength > 0.01

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

# Operation Specifications
IonDrive::calculateAcceleration
Summary: Calculates the acceleration of the ion drive.
Algorithm:
  1. If isActive is true and fuelMass > 0, return thrust / fuelMass
  2. Otherwise, return 0.0
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: double - acceleration in m/s²
Pre-condition: thrust and fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: Returns thrust/fuelMass if active and fuelMass > 0, otherwise 0

IonDrive::status
Summary: Returns the current status of the ion drive as a map.
Algorithm:
  1. Create map with keys: is_active, thrust, fuel_mass, acceleration
  2. Populate with current values
Related Features: isActive, thrust, fuelMass
Related Classes: EMap
Input: None
Output: EMap containing keys: "is_active" (boolean), "thrust" (double), "fuel_mass" (double), "acceleration" (double)
Pre-condition: isActive, thrust, fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: Returns a map with the specified keys and current values

IonDrive::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel based on thrust, specific impulse, and time.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate fuelConsumed = thrust * time / (specificImpulse * G)
  2. If fuelMass - fuelConsumed < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false
  3. Otherwise, fuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  4. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None
Input: time - duration in seconds (positive value)
Output: double - actual fuel mass consumed
Pre-condition: time > 0, thrust >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by calculated amount (clamped to 0), isActive set to false if fuel exhausted

IonDrive::deactivate
Summary: Deactivates the ion drive propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. Set isActive = false
Related Features: isActive
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: isActive is set to false

IonDrive::simulate
Summary: Simulates ion drive operation over a given duration.
Algorithm:
  1. If isActive, calculate acceleration = calculateAcceleration()
  2. Consume fuel for the duration using consumeFuel(duration)
  3. If fuel becomes zero, deactivate
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, G
Related Classes: None
Input: duration - simulation duration in seconds (positive integer)
Output: void
Pre-condition: duration >= 0
Post-condition: Fuel is consumed, isActive updated based on fuel availability, acceleration calculated during active period

IonDrive::activate
Summary: Activates the ion drive propulsion unit.
Algorithm:
  1. If fuelMass > 0, set isActive = true
  2. Otherwise, keep isActive = false
Related Features: isActive, fuelMass
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: fuelMass must be initialized
Post-condition: isActive is set to true if fuelMass > 0, otherwise remains false

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.
```

IonDrive::calculateAcceleration
Summary: Calculates the acceleration of the ion drive.

  2. Otherwise, return 0.0

  3. Calculate acceleration using calculateAcceleration()

IonDrive::consumeFuel
Summary: Consumes fuel based on thrust, specific impulse, and time.
Algorithm:
  1. Calculate fuelConsumed = thrust * time / (specificImpulse * G)
  2. If fuelMass - fuelConsumed < 0, set fuelMass = 0 and isActive = false
  3. Otherwise, fuelMass = fuelMass - fuelConsumed
  4. Return actual fuel consumed
Related Features: fuelMass, thrust, specificImpulse, isActive, G
Related Classes: None
Input: time - duration in seconds (positive value)
Output: double - actual fuel mass consumed
Pre-condition: time > 0, thrust >= 0, specificImpulse > 0, G = 9.81
Post-condition: fuelMass is reduced by calculated amount (clamped to 0), isActive set to false if fuel exhausted

# Requirement
```text
# Requirement: KOSASIH_SpaceXplore-Core

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system provides core algorithms for an interstellar exploration platform. It covers communication reliability, laser and relay transmission, propulsion simulation, solar-sail thrust, autonomous probe navigation, biosignature detection, and sensor data collection. The common theme is lightweight simulation of spacecraft subsystems with deterministic return structures and simple physical models.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Error correction uses a Hamming (7,4) style code. Encoding accepts exactly four binary characters and returns seven bits; invalid input should produce no encoded result. The four data bits occupy positions 1, 2, 4, and 6 of the encoded layout, while parity bits occupy positions 3, 5, and 7. Decoding accepts exactly seven received bits, corrects a single-bit error using the syndrome, and returns the corrected four data bits; invalid received data should produce no decoded result.

Laser communication models signal strength as power scaled by efficiency and linearly reduced by distance, using `power * efficiency / distance`. Transmission succeeds only when the resulting signal strength is above a small threshold of `0.01`.

Ion and nuclear-thermal propulsion share the same simplified operating model. A propulsion unit can activate only when fuel mass is positive. Acceleration is thrust divided by fuel mass while active and zero while inactive. Fuel consumption over time is based on thrust, specific impulse, and standard gravity `9.81`; if fuel would become negative, it should be clamped to zero and the unit should become inactive. Propulsion status maps should use the keys `is_active`, `thrust`, `fuel_mass`, and `acceleration`.

Solar-sail propulsion produces thrust only while deployed. The default solar constant is `1361`, and thrust is proportional to solar constant, sail area, and reflectivity, divided by the speed of light. A non-deployed sail has zero thrust. Solar-sail status maps should use the keys `is_deployed` and `thrust`.

Autonomous navigation works in two-dimensional space. Direction is the normalized vector from current position to destination; if the probe is already at the destination, there is no direction to compute. Movement advances by one speed-scaled step along that direction, and destination checks should use a small numerical tolerance rather than exact floating-point equality.

Biosignature detection is probabilistic. A random detection score in the range `[0.0, 1.0)` is compared against the configured threshold; scores greater than or equal to the threshold count as detected. The higher-level detection action should tolerate arbitrary biosensor payloads without throwing.

Sensor integration should produce realistic bounded readings: temperature in `[-50, 50]`, humidity in `[0, 100]`, pressure in `[900, 1100]`, and a boolean biosensor value. Collected sensor data should use the keys `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`, and `biosensor`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

There is no separate project-specific helper class required outside the UML-defined model.

- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

}

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

public double calculateAcceleration()
{

  return 0.0;

public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}

{

    setIsActive(false);

  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

  {

  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {

    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

  }

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

public void activate()
{
  if (getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    setIsActive(true);
  }
  else
  {
    setIsActive(false);
  }
}
public void deactivate()
{
  setIsActive(false);
}
public double calculateAcceleration()
{
  if (isIsActive() && getFuelMass() > 0)
  {
    return getThrust() / getFuelMass();
  }
  return 0.0;
}
public double consumeFuel(final double time)
{
  double fuelConsumed = getThrust() * time / (getSpecificImpulse() * getG());
  if (getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed < 0)
  {
    double actualConsumed = getFuelMass();
    setFuelMass(0);
    setIsActive(false);
    return actualConsumed;
  }
  else
  {
    setFuelMass(getFuelMass() - fuelConsumed);
    return fuelConsumed;
  }
}
public void simulate(final int duration)
{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}

{
  if (isIsActive())
  {
    double acceleration = calculateAcceleration();
  }
  consumeFuel(duration);
  if (getFuelMass() == 0)
  {
    deactivate();
  }
}
